questions.question: Which set is the minimum needed to make a class a JPA entity?
options: @Entity, an @Id field and a no-argument constructor
questions.explanation: Hibernate needs the @Entity marker, a primary key field and a no-argument constructor to create objects.

questions.question: Why is EnumType.STRING safer than EnumType.ORDINAL?
options: Strings use less disk space than numbers
ORDINAL is not allowed in Spring Boot 4
STRING makes the column the primary key
Stored names stay correct even if the enum order changes
questions.explanation: Ordinal stores positions, so adding a value in the middle silently changes the meaning of old rows.

questions.question: A field is marked @Transient, set to "fresh paint", and the entity is saved. A new load by id reads the row. What does the field hold?
questions.explanation: A transient field is never written to the database, so a freshly loaded object has the default null.

questions.question: An entity is declared as public final class Bike with a two-argument constructor only. What is the problem?
options: Hibernate needs a non-final class with a no-argument constructor
The class must be named Entity
questions.explanation: Hibernate creates and fills entity objects itself, so it needs a no-argument constructor and a class it can extend.

questions.question: A developer stores a price in a double field and sees 0.30000000000000004 after adding two prices. What is the better choice?
options: Use BigDecimal with precision and scale in @Column
questions.explanation: Binary floating point cannot store many decimals exactly, while BigDecimal keeps money values exact.
